title: Mixed SLO classes: the replica's scheduler orders work, it does not create capacity
summary: Three schedulers over interactive, agent and batch traffic at 2x load. class_priority lifts interactive attainment 0.926 to 0.943 and agent pays; deadline_first over chunked prefill is longest-job-first in disguise; throughput never moves.

steps.title: sched_class: the p2c baseline with three classes, at twice the load
body: sched_fifo, sched_class and sched_deadline are route_p2c with slo_classes = interactive:0.7,agent:0.2,batch:0.1 and arrival_rps = 1120, twice the baseline. They differ in exactly one key: scheduling = fifo_chunked, class_priority or deadline_first. fifo_chunked is what the engine always did; every earlier report is a run of it.

Twice the load, because at 1.2x and 1.5x nothing separates the three: 256 replicas at batch 256 hold thirty or so sequences each, so a queue never forms at the replica and the admission order has nothing to order. The class shares are a guess per calibration section 9.1, not a measurement.
steps.look_for: The scenario panel showing scheduling, slo_classes and arrival_rps as the only keys that differ from route_p2c.

steps.title: Where a replica scheduler actually decides: inside the batch, not at its door
body: Chunked prefill spends step_token_budget = 1024 tokens a step, and fifo_chunked spends it in batch order. A 24,000-token prompt admitted one step ahead of yours is 24 steps, about a third of a second, before your first chunk. That queue is invisible in the queue depth, because everyone in it has already been admitted.

class_priority hands each step's budget to interactive prompts first, then agent, then batch, FIFO within a class; and when the cache overflows it evicts the newest batch sequence first. deadline_first hands it to the least slack: deadline minus now minus the prefill still owed at the replica's rate.
steps.look_for: Prefill tokens per step pinned at the budget on every replica: the budget is the contended resource, not the batch slots.

steps.title: Per class: interactive gains 0.926 to 0.943, and agent pays
body: Under fifo_chunked, attainment by class is interactive 0.926, agent 0.972, batch 0.997, with interactive goodput 156,563 tok/s. Under class_priority (B in the A/B view) interactive rises to 0.943 and 159,615 tok/s; agent falls 0.972 to 0.960 and 47,087 to 46,412 tok/s; batch stays at 0.997.

Batch was supposed to be what gets preempted, and it is, but its 60 s time-to-first-token target has slack to spare, so pushing it back costs it nothing. The class that actually pays is agent, whose 5 s target does not. Fleet attainment 94.2% to 95.2%, goodput 229,943 to 232,141 tok/s.
steps.look_for: Attainment up and the p99 time to first token up at the same time: interactive's improved, and the p99 now belongs to agent and batch.

steps.title: What it cannot do, and why deadline_first loses
body: Throughput is 266,101 tok/s under fifo_chunked and 265,587 under class_priority. The scheduler moved who waits; it did not change how much the fleet does, because the device time per step is set by the batch and the cost model, not by the order inside it. A scheduler orders the work a replica already holds. It cannot create capacity, and it cannot reach the queue it does not see: the view is at most max_batch entries.

deadline_first drops interactive to 0.883 and the fleet to 91.1%. Least slack first charges the prefill still owed against slack, so the 24,000-token prompts, which owe the most, look the most urgent and take the budget first: earliest-deadline-first over chunked prefill is longest-job-first in disguise. A deadline scheduler needs a cost term that penalises size, not one that rewards it.
steps.look_for: Throughput within a fifth of a percent across all three runs while per-class attainment moves by whole points.
